title: CHAPTER XIII. The Delights of Anticipation

paragraphs.en: Marilla called Anne into the house as she noticed the time and the heat outside. "It’s time for your sewing," she said, looking at the clock and out into the lazy August afternoon.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉注意到时间已经不早，外面又热，便把安妮叫进了屋。“该去缝纫了。”她说着看了看钟，望向那个懒散的八月午后。

paragraphs.en: Anne rushed in from the yard, her eyes bright and cheeks flushed. "Marilla!" she exclaimed, "There's a Sunday-school picnic next week—right near Shining Waters Field!
paragraphs.zh: 安妮从院子里冲了进来，眼睛亮晶晶的，脸颊泛着红晕。“玛丽拉！”她脱口而出，“下周有个主日学校野餐——就在闪耀之水田附近！”

paragraphs.en: And Mrs. Bell and Mrs. Lynde are making ice cream—Ice cream, Marilla!"
paragraphs.zh: 贝尔太太和林德太太正在制作冰淇淋——“冰淇淋，玛丽拉！”

paragraphs.en: "Look at the clock," Marilla said sternly. "What time did I tell you to come in?"
paragraphs.zh: “看看钟,”玛丽拉严肃地说，“我让你几点回来的，你忘了？”

paragraphs.en: "It’s two o'clock—but isn’t it wonderful about the picnic? Can I go? Please can I go?
paragraphs.zh: 现在是两点钟——不过野餐的事多好啊！我能去吗？求求您，让我去吧！

paragraphs.en: I’ve never been to a picnic—only dreamed of them."
paragraphs.zh: 我从未去过野餐，只是梦想过而已。

paragraphs.en: Marilla replied, "I told you to be here at two. It's now twenty past three. Why didn't you listen?"
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉回答说：“我让你两点到这里来，现在已经快三点了。你怎么不听我的话呢？”

paragraphs.en: Anne explained, "I meant to come on time, Marilla. Idlewild is so fascinating. And I had to tell Matthew about the picnic—he’s such a good listener.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮解释说：“我本来打算准时来的，玛丽拉。Idlewild真是太吸引人了。我还得跟马修讲一讲野餐的事——他是个很好的听众。”

paragraphs.en: Can I go please?"
paragraphs.zh: “我可以去吗？”

paragraphs.en: Marilla replied, "You must learn to resist Idlewild's charm. When I say come in at a certain time, that means now. Don’t stop to chat with Matthew on your way here.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉回答说：“你必须学会抵制Idlewild的魅力。当我让你在某个时间进来时，那就是现在的意思。别在路上还停下来和马修聊天。”

paragraphs.en: As for the picnic, you can go since you’re a Sunday-school scholar and it’s not likely I’d deny you when all the other girls are going."
paragraphs.zh: 至于野餐，既然你是星期日学校的学生，而且其他女孩都去你也不大可能被拒。

paragraphs.en: Anne hesitated, then said, "But Marilla, Diana says everyone must bring a basket of food. I can't cook, so I'd feel humiliated if I had to go without a basket."
paragraphs.zh: 安妮犹豫了一下，然后说：“但是玛丽拉，戴安娜说每个人都要带一篮子食物。我不会做饭，所以我不想去而空手拿着一篮子东西会感到很尴尬。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla replied, "Don’t worry anymore. I’ll bake you one." Anne embraced her, kissing Marilla’s sallow cheek and expressing her gratitude.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉回答说：“别再担心了，我给你烤一个。”安妮紧紧拥抱着她，在玛丽拉略显蜡黄的脸颊上亲了一下，表示感激。

paragraphs.en: Marilla, though pleased, said briskly, "Stop that nonsense. I’d rather see you following instructions. As for cooking lessons, I plan to start teaching you soon.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉虽然很高兴，但还是干脆地说：“别再胡闹了。我宁愿看到你听从吩咐。至于烹饪课，我打算很快就开始教你。”

paragraphs.en: You’re too scatterbrained, Anne. I’ve been waiting to see if you could become more steady before starting. Cooking requires focus; don’t let your thoughts wander while you work."
paragraphs.zh: 你太心不在焉了，安妮。我本来在等你变得更加稳重一些再开始做饭。烹饪需要集中注意力；工作的时候可别让思绪跑神。

paragraphs.en: Anne quickly retrieved her patchwork and worked on it until teatime.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮迅速取回她的拼布，一直忙到茶点时间。

paragraphs.en: Anne sighed and pulled out her workbasket, sitting down before a pile of red and white fabric squares. "I don't enjoy patchwork," she said with a heavy heart. "It's just endless seams without much creativity.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮叹了口气，拿出她的绣花篮，坐在一堆红白相间的布料方块前。“我不喜欢拼布活儿，”她沉重地说，“这纯粹是无休止的缝纫，缺乏创意。”

paragraphs.en: But I'd rather be sewing here than playing all day."
paragraphs.zh: 但我宁可在这里缝纫，也不愿整天玩耍。

paragraphs.en: She missed the times she spent with Diana by the brook. "Marilla, you must come see our playhouse at Idlewild," Anne pleaded. "We've set up big moss-covered stones for seats and tree-to-tree boards as shelves.
paragraphs.zh: 她怀念与戴安娜在溪边度过的时光。“玛丽拉，你一定要来看看我们在Idlewild搭建的戏院啊，”安妮央求道，“我们用长满苔藓的大石头当座位，树枝做成的板子当作书架。”

paragraphs.en: Our dishes are broken but we imagine them whole. The piece of plate with ivy is especially beautiful."
paragraphs.zh: 我们的餐具虽已破碎，但我们想象它们完好无损。那片镶着常春藤的盘子尤其美丽。

paragraphs.en: Matthew was making a table for them. "And we named the little pool in Mr. Barry's field Willowmere," Anne added, her eyes lighting up. "I got that name from Diana’s book about the heroine who had five lovers and could faint easily.
paragraphs.zh: 马修正在为他们制作一张桌子。“我们在巴里先生的田地里给那小池塘取名叫柳林mere，”安妮补充道，眼中闪烁着光芒。“这个名称是从戴安娜的书中得到的，书中的女主人公有五个追求者，而且很容易晕倒。”

paragraphs.en: I hope it will be fine next Wednesday for the picnic."
paragraphs.zh: 我希望下星期三天气能好些，这样野餐就能顺利举行。

paragraphs.en: Anne longed to taste ice cream, which Diana described as beyond imagination. She was determined not to miss the event on Lake of Shining Waters, where they would have boats and ice cream. "I can't bear the thought of missing this picnic," she said, her voice filled with determination.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮渴望品尝冰淇淋，戴安娜形容那简直是无法想象的美味。她决心不miss在闪耀湖举行的野餐活动，在那里她们会有划船和享受冰淇淋的机会。“我简直不能忍受错过这次野餐的想法，”她说，语气坚定而坚决。

paragraphs.en: Anne talked about the picnic for ten minutes. Marilla then challenged her to remain silent for the same duration out of curiosity. Anne complied but spent the rest of the week eagerly anticipating the event, even working herself up over the weather.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮滔滔不绝地谈论野餐计划有十分钟之久。玛丽拉出于好奇，挑战她能否沉默同样长的时间。安妮答应了，但整个星期都满怀期待地盼望着这一天的到来，甚至因为天气问题而焦虑不安。

paragraphs.en: On Saturday, it rained, and Anne feared a continuous downpour until Wednesday. To calm her nerves, Marilla made her sew an extra patchwork square.
paragraphs.zh: 星期六，天公不作美，下了雨。安妮担心雨水会连绵到周三才停。为了安抚她不安的心情，玛丽拉让她缝制了一个额外的拼布方块。

paragraphs.en: At church on Sunday, when the minister announced the picnic, Anne felt a thrill of excitement. She admitted to Marilla that she had doubted its existence until then, but now believed it would happen.
paragraphs.zh: 在星期日的教堂里，当牧师宣布即将举行野餐时，安妮感到一阵兴奋。她向玛丽拉承认，直到那时她还怀疑它的存在，但现在相信它一定会发生。

paragraphs.en: Marilla sighed and said, "You set your heart too much on things, Anne." She warned that life held many disappointments for her.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉叹了口气，说：“安妮，你对事物的期望太高了。”她警告说，生活中充满了令人失望的事。

paragraphs.en: Anne disagreed, saying, "Looking forward is half the pleasure of something. You may not get what you want, but you can enjoy anticipating it."
paragraphs.zh: 安妮不同意，说：“期待本身就是某种乐趣的一半。你可能最终得不到想要的东西，但你可以享受那份期盼的乐趣。”

paragraphs.en: That day, Marilla wore her amethyst brooch to church as usual. It was a cherished possession passed down from her mother and believed too beautiful for Marilla to leave at home.
paragraphs.zh: 那天，玛丽拉像往常一样佩戴着紫水晶胸针去教堂。这枚胸针是母亲留下的珍贵遗物，大家都认为它美丽非凡，因此玛丽拉不愿将其留在家中。

paragraphs.en: Anne had admired the brooch deeply when she first saw it.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮初次见到那枚胸针时，就对其赞叹不已。

paragraphs.en: Anne admires the elegant amethyst brooch and wonders how Marilla can focus on the sermon with it on. She recalls her childhood fantasies about diamonds, imagining them as lovely purple stones before seeing a real diamond in a ring, which disappointed her. Anne then asks to hold the brooch for a moment and muses that amethysts might be like the souls of good violets.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮赞叹着那枚优雅的紫水晶胸针，心想玛丽拉怎么能专心听讲，把它戴在身上。她回想起自己童年的幻想，曾把钻石想象成可爱的紫色宝石，直到后来看到一枚戒指上的真钻，才有些失望。接着，安妮请求暂时拿过那枚胸针，并沉思着：紫水晶或许就像善良小紫罗兰的灵魂。
